title_en: Who Gets to See the Other Bids?
deck_zh: 从 Google 广告技术案里的竞价顺序，读到法院要求打开的接口。另一家服务商存在，与网站能够带着生意走过去，是两件事。
deck_en: Google's ad tech case follows an auction advantage into the design of a remedy. Another supplier's existence is not yet a publisher's usable route to it.
place_zh: Google 广告技术 · 竞价、接口与网站的选择
place_en: Google ad tech · Auctions, connections and publisher choice

historical_note_zh: 本篇回读2025年4月17日地区法院的责任意见，以及2026年9月2日救济意见和9月16日司法部说明。2026年意见依据 FindLaw 收录的法院原文，不采用网页编辑性摘要。这里不报告此后判决文本、上诉、执行或市场效果；历史上的 Last Look 不被描述成所有现行拍卖的规则。
historical_note_en: This reading uses the district court's 17 April 2025 liability opinion, its 2 September 2026 remedies opinion as reproduced by FindLaw, and the Justice Department's 16 September account. The reproduced judicial text, not editorial summaries, is the source. Subsequent judgments, appeals, implementation and market effects are outside its scope. Historical Last Look is not presented as the rule of every current auction.
body_zh: 一场竞价里，有一方可以先知道别人的最高报价，再调整自己的报价。它不必每次都报出原本愿意付的最高价，只要知道这次要超过多少。这种优势，不写在网页上最后出现的那张广告里。
这不是替某位网站经营者编的遭遇。2025年4月17日，美国弗吉尼亚东区联邦地区法院在 Google 广告技术案的判决意见中，写到了名为 Last Look 的安排：Google 的广告交易所 AdX，能够利用来自竞争交易所的最高报价，再决定自己的出价。[1]
先把角色分清。网站有可以出售的广告位，广告主想让广告出现在那里；交易所组织买卖双方的报价，网站一侧还需要广告服务器，决定不同来源的广告机会怎样比较和交付。Google 的 DFP 属于后一种工具，AdX 是交易所，它们不是同一个东西。广告主的购买工具，又是另外一个位置。[1]
如果把这些统统叫作 Google 广告，读者很容易只看见一家大公司与许多小公司。真正值得读的，却是不同位置之间怎样接上：谁能够把报价送进来，谁知道其他地方报了多少，谁决定最后怎样比较。规模的后果，往往发生在这些不显眼的连接处。
## 一个广告位背后的工作
广告能为网站带来收入，这件事并不因为出现垄断争议就失去价值。内容的制作、维护与传播需要资源；广告主也需要找到愿意看见自己产品的人。能够把原本很难相遇的双方接起来，是一种真实的工作。
把几项工具放在同一套系统里，也有实际的吸引力。网站不必为每个连接从头摸索，广告主可以接触更多合适的展示机会。顺手、稳定、能够获得收入，都可能是经营者选择一套工具的理由，而不只是被迫留下的表象。
Google 在2025年9月的公开回应中，正是这样反对司法部提出的拆分方案：它认为拆开整合工具会妨碍网站获得收入、提高广告主接触客户的成本，尤其影响小企业；它同时提出用互操作的方式，让第三方工具实时接触其广告需求。这是公司的理由与方案，不是效果已经实现的证明。[2]
这个理由应当认真听。但它没有回答所有问题。一套系统确实有用，与使用者必须接受其中每一项竞价顺序，是不同的主张。把更多买家带来，是服务；让自家的交易所在比较报价时取得别人没有的信息，又是另一个需要解释的决定。
2025年的法院意见，也没有把所有广告市场混成一个。法院认定 Google 在开放网络展示广告的出版商广告服务器市场、广告交易所市场，违法取得并维持垄断力量，并非法捆绑 DFP 与 AdX；但原告没有证明它主张的广告主广告网络相关市场，相关一项诉求被驳回。[1]
因此，这里可以说有地区法院经过审理作出的责任认定，不必一直退回“有人提出指控”。但不能把它扩写成法院认定 Google 的所有广告业务、每一次收购或所有整合都违法。这也不是另一起 Google 搜索案，两个案件的结论不能拿来互相补空白。
## 另一份报价怎样进来
为了让不同交易所真正比较报价，行业参与者发展了 header bidding，常译作头部竞价。按照法院回顾的过程，网站可以借此在 Google 原有技术安排之外向多家交易所取得实时报价，再把其中的胜出报价放回 DFP，与 AdX 比较。Prebid 是这一发展中的开源协作项目。[1]
这一步的意义，不只是多装了一段代码。网站尝试把比较放在自己能够看见的地方，让不同来源的报价先碰面，而不是只能接受一个封闭系统告诉它的结果。选择从服务商名单，变成了一次实际可以进行的比较。
然而，胜出报价再进入原有系统时，也成了 AdX 可以看到的门槛。Last Look 的问题就在这一顺序里：别的交易所已经报完，自家的交易所却能根据最高的外部报价，再调整自己的出价。[1] 它不需要读者相信某个高管的坏心，也不需要先猜一笔交易到底亏了多少，便已经有一个具体安排可以检查。
网站有时仍会因为接入 AdX 而多获得收入，这与它本来可能获得更多收入并不矛盾。多一个买家通常有帮助；但若这个买家能在别人亮牌以后再决定怎样跟进，帮助的存在，就不能替竞价条件的差别作担保。
这里的取舍也不能只从一笔拍卖看。一个竞争交易所若难以接触足够的交易，它以后能形成怎样的规模、数据和服务能力，也会受到影响。今天看似是一个顺序，长期可能影响明天还有谁能拿出可用的替代。要判断这种效果，需要市场与行为的证据，而不是只看某次成交是否比不成交更好。
法院在讨论促进竞争的理由时，确实把提供实时需求所带来的好处，与优待自家交易所的顺序分开。它没有因为整个功能带来过收入，就认可其中被挑战的每一个部分。[1] 这种区分比“整合好不好”更细，也更能指向可以改变的地方。
同样，网页上有一个关闭选项，也不自动说明网站可以不付代价地不用它。若撤掉一项安排，会同时失去重要买家，经营者是在比较什么、放弃什么，必须一起说明。否则，我们只是把菜单上的选择，当成了生意里的路。
## 接口开了，路就通了吗
认定过去的做法违法，接下来怎么办？2026年9月2日的救济意见没有采用出售 AdX 等结构性方案，而选择经过修改的行为性救济。法院认为这些措施足以恢复竞争；这是法院对方案的判断，不是几年后的市场成绩。[3]
Google 曾主张，互操作能够处理问题，拆分却会伤及有用的整合；原告则认为，仅靠行为规则不足以排除再次规避的风险。救济阶段的分歧，使问题从“该不该改变”走到了“怎样改变才真的有用”。裁判选择其中一种路径，也没有使另一种风险从此不存在。[2][3]
意见要求推进 AdX、DFP 与 Prebid 的连接，以及 AdX 向其他出版商广告服务器提供实时报价的连接；还涉及网站自己的历史、配置和竞价数据的取得与导出。司法部在9月16日的说明中，也强调互操作、数据可携与不歧视竞价等要求。[3][4]
这些词听起来像后台维护，落到网站经营者身上却很直接：换掉一项工具以后，重要买家的报价还能不能过来？过去的记录能否带走？另一家服务商能不能读懂，并把它用起来？若这些条件没有改变，一张允许更换服务商的声明，可能仍把人留在原处。
打开接口也不是免除技术工作。连接是否及时、稳定，传递的信息是否足够，接入需要多少成本，都可能改变这条路能否使用。尤其不能把技术上存在一次连接，直接当成双方已经可以在实质相当的条件下竞争。
这也解释了为什么监督不能只检查文件里有没有出现互操作几个字。要看的，是外部工具能完成什么，发生故障以后谁回应，网站能不能拿到足够的记录指出问题。承诺可以写得一样，日常使用却仍可能很不一样。
法院的救济意见安排了监督员与技术委员会，并以六年作为判决期限；司法部的说明也列出这项监督安排。[3][4] 监督者不是新的万能经营者。他需要技术能力，也需要在发现偏差时有办法要求解释与纠正，而他自己的权限、依据与表现也应当能够受到检查。
这里要特别留住时间上的区别。2026年的意见确定了救济路径，后面还涉及形成判决文本及具体落实。公布一份意见，不等于所要求的接口当天全部建好；读到一项义务，也不等于已经测量了它对网站收入的影响。本篇停在这些公开意见与说明，不替后续执行提前交成绩单。
对普通读者来说，这件事也不只属于做广告的人。很多看似可以更换的服务，都依赖几处平时看不见的连接：资料带不带得走，原有客户或交易伙伴能否继续接上，另一套工具有没有公平取得所需信息的办法。找到这些连接，才比较接近问题真正发生的位置。
我们不必因此要求每个网站经营者都成为拍卖工程师。好的安排，恰恰应当让人能够借助专业工作，而不是因为不会重建后台，就只能接受后台的一切条件。外部检查和可验证的接口，是把选择做出来的工作，不是选择以外的装饰。
读者在网页上看到的，仍只是一张广告。但从那张广告往后多看一步，就会发现，胜出并不总是只由谁愿意出更多钱决定。谁能先看见报价，谁负责比较，以及谁能让另一条交易之路真正接通，也在决定最后有哪些选择。
body_en: In the arrangement described by the court, Google's ad exchange could see the highest bid from competing exchanges and then adjust its own offer. A publisher might receive more than that outside bid without receiving as much as a genuinely even-handed contest could have produced. The advertisement eventually displayed on the page did not reveal the difference.[1]

This was Last Look, examined in the district court's 17 April 2025 opinion in the Google ad tech case. It is a historical arrangement in a specific record, not a description of every auction running today. Its importance is easier to understand once we separate the jobs hidden behind the expression online advertising.[1]

A publisher has advertising space. Advertisers want opportunities to reach readers. Exchanges organize bids, while a publisher ad server helps compare and deliver advertising opportunities on the website's side. Google's DFP was a publisher ad server; AdX was an exchange. Advertisers' buying tools occupied another position. One corporate name covered several different jobs.[1]

The connections among those jobs matter as much as the names. Who can deliver a bid? Who learns what another source offered? Who controls the final comparison? Thinking only of a large company facing smaller companies can miss the particular design choices through which size becomes consequential.
## Useful work, disputed conditions

Advertising can support the work of publishing. Producing material, maintaining a site and making it available all require resources; an advertiser needs a way to find an audience. Bringing those parties together is a service, not merely a convenient explanation invented after litigation began. Its usefulness should remain visible when its conditions are challenged.

Integration has an intelligible appeal too. A publisher does not have to build every connection itself. Advertisers can find opportunities through familiar tools, and some of the work of comparison and delivery is handled within one system. Ease, reliability and revenue can be genuine reasons for choosing it, rather than evidence that the chooser has been deceived.

Google made that argument against the Justice Department's proposed breakup in September 2025. It said separation would make monetizing content harder and reaching customers more expensive, particularly for small businesses. Its own proposal emphasized interoperability, allowing third-party tools real-time access to advertiser bids. These were the company's arguments and proposed solution, not an independent assessment of their eventual effects.[2]

The argument merits a serious hearing. But useful integration and the necessity of a particular auction advantage are different propositions. Bringing additional buyers is one contribution. Giving an affiliated exchange information its rivals lack is a further decision. The contribution cannot, by itself, justify every condition attached to obtaining it.

The district court did not treat all advertising as one market. It found unlawful monopolization of open-web display publisher ad servers and ad exchanges, and unlawful tying of DFP and AdX. The advertiser-ad-network claim failed because the plaintiffs had not established the relevant market they proposed. The finding was bounded, not a verdict against all Google advertising.[1]

That distinction affects how we can tell the story. These were liability findings after trial, not merely allegations surviving an early motion. Yet they do not establish that every acquisition, every integrated function or every advertising product was unlawful. Nor is this the separate Google Search case, whose results cannot be imported to complete an argument here.
## Getting another bid into the room

Publishers and other industry participants developed header bidding to obtain real-time offers from multiple exchanges outside Google's existing architecture. Prebid was an open-source collaborative effort in that development. The winning outside bid could then enter DFP as a floor against which AdX competed. An alternative comparison had become technically possible.[1]

That was more than adding another supplier's name to a list. It moved part of the comparison to a place publishers could inspect. Instead of relying entirely on a closed system's account of the result, a publisher could arrange for competing sources to meet and examine what happened. Choice acquired a means of being exercised.

But the winning outside offer also revealed a threshold. Under Last Look, AdX could respond after competing exchanges had already submitted their bids.[1] The significant detail is the order of operations. We need not invent an executive's private motive or a particular publisher's losses to identify something concrete requiring an explanation.

There is no contradiction in a publisher benefiting from AdX demand while still receiving less than a more even contest might yield. An additional buyer can be helpful. That does not establish that the buyer needs an opportunity to inspect the best competing offer before responding. The useful service and the informational advantage have to be evaluated separately.

The question also extends beyond one sale. If competing exchanges have difficulty winning transactions, their ability to develop scale, data and services may suffer. A present auction design can affect who will be capable of offering a credible alternative later. Establishing that effect requires market evidence, not simply an observation that one transaction was better than no transaction.

The liability opinion itself separated the benefits of introducing real-time advertiser demand from the challenged preferences within the arrangement.[1] That is a more workable inquiry than deciding whether integration is good or bad in the abstract. It directs attention to what a system could retain while changing a particular condition.

An apparent option to switch off a feature needs the same scrutiny. If doing so also gives up access to important buyers, a publisher is choosing between packages, not deciding about one isolated setting. Both the value retained and the value lost belong in the account. A choice on a menu is not necessarily an economically usable route.
## An open connection is a task, not a slogan

After liability came the harder question of remedy. In its 2 September 2026 opinion, the court rejected structural remedies including an AdX sale and chose modified behavioral measures. It judged those measures sufficient to restore competition. That was a judicial assessment of a remedial design, not a measurement of a market years after implementation.[3]

Google had argued that interoperability could address the problem without disrupting useful integration. The plaintiffs argued that conduct rules would not adequately prevent evasion and sought structural change as well. Their disagreement mattered even though many proposed behavioral provisions overlapped. Selecting a remedy does not make its risks cease to exist.[2][3]

The opinion required connections between AdX, DFP and Prebid, access to AdX real-time bids through rival publisher ad servers, and ways for publishers to obtain and export their own data. The Justice Department's 16 September explanation likewise emphasized interoperability, data portability and nondiscriminatory bidding. These were specified obligations and objectives, not evidence that every integration already worked.[3][4]

Translated from the technical language, the questions are recognizable. After replacing a tool, can the publisher still receive important bids? Can it take its records and configuration with it? Can another provider understand and use what arrives? Permission to choose a rival is of limited assistance if the business cannot make the journey.

Building that route requires work. A connection may exist but be too slow, unreliable, costly or incomplete to support comparable service. Checking that an interface has been announced is therefore not equivalent to checking that another provider can compete through it. The quality of the connection belongs inside the remedy, not outside as an incidental engineering detail.

The same is true of information. Exporting a file is only the beginning if the recipient cannot interpret it or integrate it into an operating system. Documentation, technical support and usable formats are part of making portability real. Otherwise the publisher may formally possess its records while remaining dependent on the original provider to make sense of them.

This is where oversight has to look beyond promises. What can an outside tool actually do? What happens when it fails to obtain information? Can a publisher produce enough of a record to show the discrepancy and receive an answer? Identically worded commitments can conceal markedly different conditions in everyday use.

The remedies opinion provided for a monitor and technical committee and selected a six-year judgment term; the department's account also described that oversight.[3][4] A monitor is not an infallible substitute operator. It needs relevant competence and a route from identifying a problem to requiring a response. Its own reach, evidence and performance should remain examinable too.

The dates must stay distinct from the outcome. The opinion set a remedial path, with further work on the judgment's text and implementation. Publication did not mean the required interfaces were built that day. An obligation to provide access is not a measured increase in publisher revenue. This reading stops at the public opinions and September explanation, rather than issuing a premature implementation report.

The disagreement over structural and behavioral remedies remains worth understanding on its own terms. A forced separation can create transition difficulties; an ongoing conduct regime requires capable, durable supervision. Neither concern is answered by announcing that competition is desirable. A remedy must explain how its particular design addresses the established harm and what will make its commitments effective.

The wider lesson is not restricted to advertising. Many services that appear replaceable depend on connections people rarely see: whether records can travel, whether trading partners can remain reachable, and whether a new tool can obtain the information needed to function. Looking for those connections often gets closer to the point where a nominal option becomes a practical dependency.

This does not require every publisher to become an auction engineer. A useful arrangement should allow people to rely on professional work without making their inability to rebuild the machinery a reason to accept every condition it imposes. Verifiable connections and external review are ways of constructing choice, not decorations added after choice already exists.

The reader of a webpage still sees an advertisement. Behind it lie decisions about whose offers arrived, who could inspect them and who performed the comparison. The case invites us to look at those decisions without declaring all integration suspect: not only whether another route has a name, but whether anyone has done the work needed to connect it.
